what_it_does: The C2 application layer is the software commanders and staffs actually touch: it (1) renders a common operational picture (COP) from friendly-force position reports (PLI), enemy tracks, graphics/overlays and unit status; (2) supports deliberate and crisis planning (MDMP/JPP) producing orders, synchronization matrices, task organizations and COAs; (3) coordinates and deconflicts fires (AFATDS/AXS), airspace (TAIS, ACO/ATO), air and missile defense (AMDWS/IBCS), deep-operations targeting (JADOCS/JTIC2S) and sustainment (GCSS-Army, TyrOS); (4) manages tasks, requests for information and reports across a headquarters battle rhythm; (5) pushes orders and situational awareness down to mounted (MMC/JBC-P) and dismounted (ATAK/Nett Warrior/SBMC) users; and (6) increasingly hosts decision aids (Maven Smart System, Thunderforge, JSDT). It sits above the data layer/data fabric (S02) and transport (S05) and depends on both; in 2025-2026 the Army (NGC2), Navy (Overmatch), DAF (Battle Network/CBC2/KRADOS) and Space Force (Kobayashi Maru) are all converging toward architectures in which a government-owned or vendor-led integrated data layer exposes APIs and third-party apps plug in, rather than each warfighting function owning a stovepiped program of record.

current_architecture.description: Two generations coexist. Legacy: warfighting-function programs of record (AFATDS, TAIS, AMDWS, JADOCS, GCCS-A/J, CPOF then CPCE/Command Web, JBC-P then MMC) each with its own server stack, message formats and ATO, converged over 2018-2023 into CPCE for the command post and MMC for vehicles. Emerging (2024-2026): NGC2 as an 'ecosystem of transport, infrastructure, data and applications' where a common data layer (Anduril Lattice edge-to-cloud mesh, Palantir Foundry cloud data layer, Raft data/services registries and federation, established as the Army baseline June 22 2026) exposes APIs to applications from many vendors (Onebrief planning, Accelint/Lyntris mission command interface, Govini, Striveworks, Instant Connect, Research Innovations, Shift5 telemetry, Rune TyrOS logistics, Microsoft cloud). Legacy PoRs are being re-hosted (AFATDS 7.0 Java rewrite, AXS microservices, containerized MMC-Software and JTIC2S) and forced to expose APIs (Operation Jailbreak / 'Right to Integrate', May 2026: ~600 participants, >50 companies, APIs documented across >70 Army capabilities including IBCS-M). Navy (Overmatch), DAF (Battle Network with CBC2 and KRADOS) and Space Force (Kobayashi Maru) follow the same pattern with government software factories as integrators. TAK remains the de facto dismounted/mobile SA client across services and agencies, with an open plugin model.

The Sept 2025 Army CTO memo found NGC2 prototype lacked role-based access control and audit logging so 'any user can potentially access and misuse sensitive' classified information; remediation was claimed by the Army CIO.
current_architecture.connectivity_dependency: High. NGC2 is cloud-native with edge compute (Anduril Voyager Tactical Edge Compute ran the full stack in vehicles 'disconnected when required' at Ivy Sting 5); Onebrief and Maven are web apps requiring at least intermittent links; private 5G served as primary transport for calls for fire at Lightning Surge 2 with satellite radios secondary.
current_architecture.what_breaks_when_disconnected: Cloud-hosted planning and Foundry-side analytics stall; COPs go stale and diverge between nodes until resync; staffs revert to voice, chat and paper. NGC2 design goal is DDIL operation per echelon with local compute and data mesh replication, but an industry critique (LinkedIn, 2026) argued vendors still treat DDIL as an edge case rather than the baseline; Joint Staff budget language since FY2019 stresses 'denied-disconnected, intermittent, low-bandwidth' capability at CJTF level as an unmet demand.

technical_difficulty.summary: Building a COP or planning UI is not hard; the difficulty is (a) integrating with dozens of legacy message formats and PoRs whose APIs were only documented in 2026, (b) keeping state consistent across DDIL nodes (conflict-free replication, bandwidth-aware sync, local compute), (c) meeting Army cybersecurity expectations (RBAC, audit logging, supply-chain scanning) that the flagship prototype itself failed in Sept 2025, and (d) surviving the ATO/accreditation and network-access process. Domain fidelity (doctrinal workflows, symbology, fires safety) is a hard requirement that generic SaaS teams underestimate.

technical_difficulty.hardest_problem: Bidirectional, trusted integration between a planning/COP app and execution systems (AFATDS/AXS, TAIS, IBCS-M, GCSS-Army) under DDIL conditions without manual re-entry, while preserving fires-safety semantics and classification/releasability rules.

why_not_solved.explanation: Until 2025-2026 each warfighting-function PoR owned its data and interfaces; the Army had to run Operation Jailbreak to force API exposure. Third parties could not integrate without the prime's cooperation.

ATO, network access and facility clearance are the 'three barriers' cited by Onebrief's founder; the flagship NGC2 prototype itself failed a security assessment, which will make authorizing officials stricter, not looser, about third-party apps.
Buyers are split across PEOs, DIU, CDAO, service software factories and units with GPC cards; a $25k pilot does not lead to a program line without a sponsor who owns budget.
Fires/airspace semantics, message standards and classification rules make plan-to-execution automation risky; nobody wants software that mis-clears airspace.

COP/SA is commoditized (TAK, Lattice, Maven); HQ-level planning is being solved by Onebrief; data-layer plumbing is now owned by Anduril/Palantir/Raft under Army designation. Remaining whitespace is narrower than the headline budgets suggest.
Prototype OTAs are small ($26M-$100M for whole teams) and split among many members; sustained revenue depends on production decisions the Army has not scheduled (GAO).

attractiveness.bull: Largest, most visible C2 modernization in decades with explicit third-party app ecosystems (NGC2 CSO with rolling windows, Jailbreak API marketplace, TAK Third Party Pipeline, Overmatch Software Armory), FY26-27 requests in the billions, unit-level buyers who iterate with vendors in days, and proof that a 2019 startup (Onebrief) can reach $2B+ valuation and an Army enterprise contract on a single workflow wedge. AI/agentic staff tooling is the fastest-growing budget line.
attractiveness.bear: The platform and data layers are now assigned (Anduril, Palantir, Raft) and the planning layer is claimed (Onebrief); remaining openings are components inside someone else's stack with small dollar values, dependent on team leads and a production timeline GAO says does not exist. Security scrutiny after the 2025 memo raises the bar for unknown vendors. Access constraints (ITAR, clearances, FOCI) are severe for a team with a non-U.S.-person founder and a student-scale budget. Absence of visible competitors in a niche is not evidence of demand.
attractiveness.verdict: Medium overall for a well-connected U.S. team; low-to-medium for these founders. Enter only through an existing on-ramp (TAK plugin, Lattice SDK component, NGC2 CSO component proposal, Jailbreak-style sprint) with a narrow workflow wedge, or target allied/public-safety TAK users first.
